why: 200 before, 403 with the allow-list armed, 200 again after restoring it -- same path, same credential, same run, one variable. The refusing policy named ITSELF in the response body, so this is a positive attribution rather than the absence of a competing one (B-44, B-46). And the reversal rules out 'the config change broke the route', which a two-phase test could not have distinguished.

observed_client_ip_finding.why_it_matters: This is the address Gravitee's ip-filtering policy compares against the allow-list. It is NOT the address Databricks sees: Databricks sees this host's public NAT address, while the gateway -- a container on the same host as the client -- sees a private one. Two controls both called 'the IP allow-list', keyed on addresses from different address spaces. 11.7 B-35 argued this; this is the measurement.
observed_client_ip_finding.generator_consequence: scripts/29_gen_gravitee_route_family.py defines LOCAL_TEST_CIDR = 172.21.0.0/16 and ADDS it to the allow-list whenever a recipient's ip_access_list_mode is APPLIED. The observed client address falls inside that CIDR. So every allow-list the generator emits in APPLIED mode admits the whole Docker bridge network -- which is every client that can reach the gateway from this host. The control is vacuous in exactly the configuration that is supposed to enforce it.
observed_client_ip_finding.near_miss: T-03 would have reported ALLOW_LIST_NOT_ENFORCED if it had used t02-iplist -- the recipient whose allow-list is APPLIED -- because that list contains LOCAL_TEST_CIDR and this client is inside it. The subject was chosen for a different reason (t02-iplist has no reachable 200 control), so the test passed by luck of subject selection, not by the control working everywhere.
observed_client_ip_finding.severity: A test accommodation that silently disables the control under test, in a file whose whole purpose is to be the deployable source of truth for AC6 / T-12 'redeploy from code'. If promoted, the allow-list ships open.

edge_is_not_the_only_door.observed: edge 403, direct 200, same credential, same window
edge_is_not_the_only_door.meaning: The edge allow-list controls access THROUGH THE EDGE. It does not control access to the share. The same bearer token read the same data over the open internet while the edge was refusing it.
edge_is_not_the_only_door.not_a_defect_in: Gravitee, which did exactly what it was told
edge_is_not_the_only_door.conops_consequence: §2.3.2 reads as though the edge allow-list is a control over access. AC2's acceptance text should say 'refused at the edge' rather than 'refused', and v1.6 should state which of the two allow-lists -- the gateway's or the Databricks-side one -- is the control of record for address-based refusal. Only the second can close the direct path, and 11.7 B-38 / D-8 show it gates its own enrolment.

what_this_does_not_prove: T-02. The Databricks-side IP access list is a different control at a different layer and was not touched. The two allow-lists do not observe the same address: Databricks sees this host's public NAT address, the gateway sees a private one.
That the allow-list protects the DATA. See edge_is_not_the_only_door when present.
